locations.name: Mongbwalu Health Zone
locations.notes: Believed index origin of the outbreak; a busy mining area where MSF found 55 deaths since early April; three health areas affected.

locations.name: Rwampara Health Zone
locations.notes: Six health areas affected; site of the INRB sampling that yielded 8 PCR-positive samples confirming Bundibugyo virus on 15 May 2026.

locations.name: Bunia Health Zone
locations.notes: Provincial capital; index suspected case (a healthcare worker) died here on 24 April 2026; MSF Salama clinic has isolated suspected cases.

locations.name: Kampala
locations.notes: Two unlinked imported cases confirmed on 15–16 May 2026 in individuals travelling from DRC; one fatality (59-year-old Congolese man, Kibuli Muslim Hospital); no local transmission confirmed as of reporting.

locations.name: Goma
locations.notes: INRB-confirmed case on 17 May 2026: wife of a Bunia Ebola fatality who travelled to rebel-held Goma while symptomatic; raises cross-provincial and Rwanda border risk.

locations.name: Beni
locations.notes: UN News reported an individual who travelled from Bunia to Beni tested positive for Ebola; under investigation.

timeline.event: Index case — a nurse — presents with fever, hemorrhage, vomiting and malaise at a medical centre in Bunia, Ituri Province, DRC; later dies. (WHO DON602 / DRC MoH)

Suspected index case — a nurse at Evangelical Medical Centre, Bunia — develops fever, bleeding, and severe weakness; dies within days. Retrospective investigation suggests she was infected by a patient, implying community transmission was already ongoing.
Earliest known suspected case — a healthcare worker in Bunia — reports symptom onset (fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting); dies at Bunia medical centre. (WHO DON602)
Cluster of unexplained haemorrhagic fever deaths flagged in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, DRC.
WHO alerted to a high-mortality outbreak of unknown etiology in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including deaths of four health workers within four days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including deaths among healthcare workers; initial GeneXpert tests in Bunia return negative for Zaire Ebola.
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness cluster in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 healthcare worker deaths within 4 days. (WHO DON602)
MSF receives alerts of increased hemorrhagic fever deaths in Mongbwalu; team deployed finds 55 deaths since early April. (MSF statement)
Rapid-response teams investigate Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZs; 13 blood samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa for advanced analysis. (WHO DON602)
WHO rapid-response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones. (WHO DON602)
INRB Kinshasa analyses samples; PCR confirms Orthoebolavirus in 8 of 13 specimens; genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). (WHO DON602 / INRB)
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 confirmed Orthoebolavirus-positive by PCR on 15 May. Second Uganda imported case confirmed in Kampala on 16 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara; 8 test positive by PCR for Orthoebolavirus. (WHO DON602)
Bundibugyo virus confirmed by laboratory (8 of 13 samples positive). First confirmed case detected in Kampala, Uganda.

DRC Ministry of Public Health officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak; Uganda MoH confirms imported BVD case — 59-year-old Congolese male who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, on 2026-05-14. (DRC MoH / Uganda MoH / Africa CDC)
Africa CDC activates Incident Management Support Team; convenes urgent cross-border coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan, WHO and partners. (Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak; INRB confirms 8 positive samples by PCR, genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case — a 59-year-old Congolese man who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala.

INRB genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). DRC MoH officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (died 14 May in Kampala). Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination call. (WHO DON602; Africa CDC)
Second confirmed Kampala case (fatal). Suspected Kinshasa case reported (later retracted).
Second imported confirmed case identified in Kampala with no apparent link to the first; suspected Kinshasa case tests negative on confirmatory INRB PCR and is disconfirmed. (WHO PHEIC / INRB)
WHO Director-General determines the Bundibugyo outbreak in DRC and Uganda constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC); does not meet pandemic emergency criteria. (WHO)

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC for Bundibugyo Ebola in DRC and Uganda; determination cites 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in Ituri plus 2 confirmed cases in Kampala and 4 HCW deaths. Africa CDC holds 130-participant high-level consultative meeting.

Second imported case confirmed in Kampala (unlinked to first). WHO Director-General determines outbreak constitutes a PHEIC. 246 suspected cases, 80 suspected deaths in Ituri confirmed at this time-point. (WHO PHEIC declaration)
WHO Director-General declares Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

INRB/AFP confirms Goma case: wife of a Bunia Ebola fatality tested positive after traveling to Goma (North Kivu) while already infected, extending geographic spread beyond Ituri. (INRB via AFP / Al Jazeera)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Bundibugyo virus disease; CDC and US State Dept coordinate medical evacuation to Germany for treatment; 6 additional high-risk contacts also moved to Germany. (CDC / NBC News)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Ebola Bundibugyo; US officials coordinate evacuation of seven individuals to Germany for care. CDC confirms Level 2 travel health notice for DRC, Level 1 for Uganda.
WHO Emergency Committee to be convened; WHO Director-General confirms PHEIC declared without prior Emergency Committee recommendation — a first in WHO history, citing extraordinary urgency.
WHO formally announces PHEIC; does not declare pandemic emergency. INRB confirms first case in Goma (North Kivu) — wife of Bunia fatality. (WHO; INRB via AFP)
US missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus at Nyankunde Hospital near Bunia; CDC confirms an American has tested positive. (Serge charity; CDC briefing)
Outbreak expands from 3 to 9+ health zones in DRC. New confirmed case in Goma (under M23 rebel control). US CDC enacts enhanced travel screening.
Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); reports ~395 suspected cases and 106 associated deaths across DRC and Uganda. (Africa CDC)

CDC and DHS implement enhanced US travel screening, Title 42 entry restrictions on non-US passport holders who traveled to DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in the prior 21 days; CDC EOC activated. (CDC / DHS)

CDC Situation Summary (most recent official update) reports 11 confirmed cases and 336 suspected cases including 88 deaths in DRC, and 2 confirmed cases including 1 death in Uganda across 9 health zones. (CDC Situation Summary)

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths confirmed. US CDC/DHS invoke Title 42, restricting entry of non-US passport holders who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in prior 21 days.

Ebola confirmed in Goma, North Kivu (rebel-held M23 city); Rwanda closes Goma-Gisenyi border crossings. Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. DRC Health Minister announces three new Ebola treatment centres opening in Ituri.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3(F) of Africa CDC Statute. 395 suspected cases, 106 associated deaths reported. (Africa CDC PHECS declaration)

CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 travel restrictions; entry restrictions placed on non-US passport holders from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan in previous 21 days. CDC moves 7 Americans (1 confirmed case + 6 high-risk contacts) to Germany for care. (CDC)
CDC current situation page confirms 9 health zones in Ituri Province now affected; EU announces PPE stockpiles ready for deployment and detection kit support to Africa CDC. (CDC; CNN)

OCHA reports 482+ suspected cases since April in Ituri; confirms Goma case; warns hostile environment (insecurity, displacement, hunger) is severely hampering response; >5 tonnes of supplies airlifted to Ituri by WFP.
UN News and NBC report outbreak approaching ~500 suspected cases and 116 associated deaths; case in Beni (North Kivu) also reported; situation remains rapidly evolving.

alerts.title: PHEIC declared — Bundibugyo Ebola, DRC & Uganda
alerts.body: On 16–17 May 2026 the WHO Director-General determined this outbreak constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) but not a pandemic emergency. No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus.

alerts.title: Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security
alerts.body: Africa CDC declared a PHECS on 18 May 2026, empowering continent-wide coordination. As of that declaration, 395 suspected cases and 106 associated deaths have been reported across DRC and Uganda.

alerts.title: Outbreak spreads to Goma (North Kivu) and Beni — Rwanda border at risk
alerts.body: INRB confirmed a case in rebel-held Goma on 17 May (wife of a Bunia fatality who travelled while symptomatic), and a case in Beni on 18 May; Rwanda-DRC border is on high alert.

alerts.title: US invokes Title 42 travel restrictions; American healthcare worker infected
alerts.body: On 18 May 2026, CDC and DHS invoked Title 42 entry restrictions on travellers from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. A US missionary physician tested positive on 17 May and is being evacuated to Germany along with 6 high-risk contacts.

alerts.title: 9 health zones affected in Ituri Province — rapid geographic expansion
alerts.body: As of 18 May 2026, CDC confirms the outbreak has spread to 9 health zones in Ituri Province, up from 3 at initial declaration. True caseload is believed substantially higher than confirmed figures.

alerts.title: No approved Bundibugyo vaccine; candidate therapeutics in pre-clinical stage only
alerts.body: WHO, CDC, and MSF confirm no licensed vaccines or specific antivirals exist for Bundibugyo virus. CEPI awarded Moderna and Oxford $26.7 M in Jan 2026 to develop candidates; a Chinese mRNA vaccine has shown efficacy in mice but has not reached primate or human trials.

news.title: Ebola outbreak grows to ~500 suspected cases; UN reports 116 deaths as of May 19
news.summary: The UN reported on Monday that the DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has grown to nearly 500 suspected cases and 116 deaths. An American missionary confirmed positive is being evacuated to Germany for treatment along with 6 high-risk contacts.

news.title: Africa CDC declares Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a continental security emergency
news.summary: Africa CDC invoked its PHECS designation on 18 May 2026, reporting 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths across DRC and Uganda. The declaration allows Africa CDC to lead and resource a continent-wide coordinated response.

news.title: US CDC invokes Title 42 travel restrictions; evacuates exposed Americans to Germany
news.summary: CDC and DHS on 18 May imposed entry restrictions on non-US passport holders who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within 21 days. Seven Americans, including one confirmed Ebola case, are being transferred to Germany for care and quarantine.

news.title: American missionary Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo Ebola in DRC
news.summary: Dr. Stafford, a physician with Christian nonprofit Serge treating patients at Nyankunde Hospital near Bunia, tested positive on 17 May. His wife and colleague were exposed but asymptomatic; the family is preparing evacuation to Germany.

news.title: Reuters explainer: What do we know about the Bundibugyo Ebola strain?
news.summary: Reuters details that no approved vaccines or drugs exist for Bundibugyo virus; candidate therapeutics including Merck's Ervebo and Mapp Biopharmaceutical's MBP134 have shown promise in non-human primates but remain unapproved. NanoViricides' NV-387 antiviral is in early-stage clinical trials.

news.title: Bloomberg: American missionary tests positive; US bans travel from stricken area
news.summary: A US missionary confirmed positive for Ebola in DRC is showing symptoms and being sent to Germany for treatment, CDC incident manager Satish Pillai confirmed. Six additional Americans with possible exposure are also being relocated to Germany.

news.title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DRC and Uganda a global health emergency
news.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros declared the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak a PHEIC on 16–17 May 2026, citing cross-border spread, a high sample positivity rate, and the absence of approved vaccines. The outbreak does not meet pandemic emergency criteria.

news.title: Ebola confirmed in Goma: wife of Bunia victim carried virus to North Kivu
news.summary: INRB director Prof. Jean-Jacques Muyembe confirmed a positive case in rebel-held Goma on 17 May — the wife of a man who died of Ebola in Bunia, who travelled while already infected. The Rwanda-DRC border went on high alert.

news.title: CNN: Over 100 deaths and no approved vaccine — what to know about the Ebola PHEIC
news.summary: CNN reports more than 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths as of 19 May 2026 after Africa CDC's PHECS declaration; no approved vaccine or therapeutic exists for Bundibugyo. MSF emergency program manager called the spread 'extremely concerning.'

news.title: Ebola outbreak in Ituri follows DRC hunger and displacement crisis — UN
news.summary: UN News reports the Ebola emergency is unfolding against a pre-existing catastrophic humanitarian crisis in DRC's east; aid cuts are cited as having weakened surveillance, allowing the outbreak to grow undetected for weeks.

news.title: Imperial College London experts: This is already the largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever
news.summary: Imperial College School of Public Health experts note that with 246+ suspected cases this outbreak surpasses all previous Bundibugyo outbreaks combined, ranking 7th largest across all Ebola species, and likely went undetected for weeks or months.

news.title: NPR: WHO declares Ebola in Congo a global health emergency; no vaccine for the strain
news.summary: NPR reports on the PHEIC and highlights that Africa CDC has confirmed a candidate monkey-tested experimental vaccine with ~50% efficacy but it has not been studied in human patients, leaving only supportive care as treatment.

background.virus: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV); formal species name Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense
background.discovery: 2007, during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel species
background.case_fatality_rate_historical: 25–51% (WHO historical range); MSF and Johns Hopkins experts cite 25–40% for BDBV specifically in current outbreak context
background.transmission: Direct contact with blood, body fluids, or tissues of infected people or animals; contact with contaminated surfaces or fomites. Individuals are infectious only when symptomatic.
background.symptoms: Sudden fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat — followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, rash, impaired kidney/liver function, internal and external bleeding; nosebleeds and vomiting blood reported in current outbreak.
background.vaccines_therapeutics: No WHO-approved or FDA-approved vaccines or specific therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus as of May 2026. The two licensed Ebola vaccines (Merck Ervebo, J&J Zabdeno/Mvabea) target Zaire ebolavirus and provide poor cross-protection against BDBV per animal studies. Candidate countermeasures showing promise in non-human primates include Merck Ervebo (partial), Mapp Biopharmaceutical MBP134, and Auro Vaccines VesiculoVax. NanoViricides' NV-387 antiviral (currently in mpox clinical trials) is proposed as a candidate. An mRNA multivalent vaccine targeting BDBV is in pre-clinical (mouse) stage — published in PNAS May 2026 — but has not entered primate or human trials. CEPI awarded Moderna and the University of Oxford $26.7 million in January 2026 to develop multivalent Ebola mRNA and viral vector platforms covering BDBV. All BDBV-specific candidates remain pre-licensure; supportive care is the current standard of treatment.

past_outbreaks.notes: First identified outbreak; led to the discovery and naming of the Bundibugyo strain.
Second documented Bundibugyo outbreak; contained within months in a remote area.
Second-largest Ebola outbreak in history, different species (Zaire ebolavirus), but same geographic zone and containment challenges (insecurity, mobile populations, mistrust).

past_outbreaks.notes: DRC's 16th Ebola outbreak, declared on 4 September 2025 and declared over 1 December 2025; 53 confirmed, 11 probable cases.

past_outbreaks.location: Ituri Province (epicentre), North Kivu Province, Kinshasa — DRC; Kampala — Uganda
past_outbreaks.cfr: ~27% of suspected (true CFR undetermined pending full case ascertainment)
past_outbreaks.notes: Third and largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever; declared a PHEIC on 16–17 May 2026 and a PHECS by Africa CDC on 18 May 2026; at least 9 health zones affected; no approved vaccine or therapeutic.

why_this_matters: This is the largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded, surpassing the combined case counts of the two previous BDBV outbreaks and already ranking 7th largest across all Ebola species historically.

No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus; existing licensed Ebola vaccines target Zaire ebolavirus and provide poor cross-protection, leaving response entirely dependent on classic public-health containment measures.
The outbreak zone overlaps with active armed conflict in eastern DRC (Ituri and North Kivu), severely impeding access, contact tracing, and the safe operation of treatment centres.

Cross-border spread to Uganda confirmed within days of initial detection, and a confirmed case has now reached rebel-held Goma (North Kivu), raising the risk of further regional spread into Rwanda, South Sudan, and beyond.
Healthcare worker deaths (at least 4 confirmed) and suspected hospital-acquired transmission indicate critical infection prevention and control (IPC) gaps, amplifying outbreak risk.

The outbreak likely went undetected for 3–4 weeks before reporting, partly because standard Ebola field tests (Xpert, targeting Zaire ebolavirus) returned false negatives; the true caseload is almost certainly substantially higher than official figures.
A US citizen healthcare worker has been infected, prompting US Title 42 travel restrictions and underscoring the outbreak's international reach.
Cuts to global and US public-health funding in 2025–2026 have been directly linked by public-health experts and Oxfam to the surveillance gaps that allowed this outbreak to grow undetected.
